title: Bounded classical coproduct transport through étale origins
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with the discrete topology and $f:X	o Y$ a proper morphism of schemes. Proper has the meaning of [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $T=X,Y$ let $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},A_T)$ and $D_T=D(\mathcal A_T)$ be the ordinary constant-$A$ module-sheaf categories and their unbounded derived categories, in a common universe in which the sites and all indexing families under consideration are small [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $G=Rf_{\mathrm{pro\acute et},*}$ for total K-injective direct image and use the classical-cohomology predicate of [sk-def-pe-classical-definition].
Let $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}	o T_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and let $D_{T,\mathrm{\acute et}}$ be the ordinary unbounded derived category of constant-$A$ étale module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For either $T$, every small ambient coproduct of classical-cohomology objects of $D_T$ again has classical cohomology, and their standard good truncations have classical cohomology. Ambient coproducts commute naturally with cohomology and with both good truncations, including the canonical maps $	au_{\le b}L	o L$ and $L	o	au_{\ge a}L$ [def-kun-truncations]. The exact termwise derived functor $
u_T^*:D_{T,\mathrm{\acute et}}	o D_T$ preserves all small coproducts. Put $E=Rf_{\mathrm{\acute et},*}$. Assume that $E$ preserves all small coproducts in $D_{X,\mathrm{\acute et}}$. For any integers $a\le b$ and any small family $(L_s)_{s\in I}$ of classical-cohomology objects in $D_X^{\ge a}\cap D_X^{\le b}$, there exist $B_s\in D_{X,\mathrm{\acute et}}^{\ge a}\cap D_{X,\mathrm{\acute et}}^{\le b}$ and isomorphisms $i_s:
u_X^*B_s\xrightarrow{\sim}L_s$; here and above, degree bounds refer to the standard t-structures [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Here $\iota_s:B_s	o igoplus_sB_s$ and $\iota'_s:L_s	o igoplus_sL_s$ are the specified ambient coprojections. For every such choice define $t:
u_X^*( igoplus_sB_s)\xrightarrow{\sim} igoplus_sL_s$ by $t\circ
u_X^*(\iota_s) = \iota'_s\circ i_s$. Let $\alpha_Y: igoplus_s
u_Y^*EB_s\xrightarrow{\sim}
u_Y^*( igoplus_sEB_s)$ be the canonical inverse-image sum comparison, and let $	heta_B:
u_Y^*EB\xrightarrow{\sim}G
u_X^*B$ be the value at the bounded-below object $B$ of the canonical natural transformation $
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{\acute et},*}	o Rf_{\mathrm{pro\acute et},*}
u_X^*$ of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], which that statement makes invertible on bounded-below inputs since $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then, in ordinary right-to-left composition order, the canonical coproduct comparison $\sigma_L: igoplus_sGL_s	o G( igoplus_sL_s)$ is the following specified composite:
$$\sigma_L=G(t)\circ	heta_{ igoplus_s B_s}\circ
u_Y^*(\sigma^E_B)\circ\alpha_Y\circ igoplus_s igl(	heta_{B_s}^{-1}\circ G(i_s)^{-1} igr),$$
where $\sigma^E_B: igoplus_sEB_s	o E( igoplus_sB_s)$ is the étale coproduct comparison. In particular $\sigma_L$ is invertible and its composite with the $s$-th coprojection is $G(\iota'_s)$. The factorization and closure assertions include the empty family. No unbounded étale/classical derived equivalence is asserted.

proof.text: The fixed-ring module-sheaf categories carry the existing Grothendieck and K-injective structures. Apply [src-weil-derived-homology-preserves-coproducts] to get preservation of ambient coproducts by every derived homology functor. This is the original cohomology computation, already formalized in HomologyCoproducts.lean. The coproduct universal property implies that common lower and upper cohomological bounds are preserved (isGE_sigma and isLE_sigma). No boundedness is used for the homology assertion.

The exact coefficient realization has underlying abelian sheaf isomorphic to the original fixed-ring module sheaf: its sheafification counit is invertible. Combine this with the homology isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]. Thus realized classical cohomology is equivalent degreewise to classicality of the underlying fixed-ring module cohomology. standardHomologyIso only transports between small-Hom and standard localizations.

By [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules], each classical cohomology sheaf is comparison inverse image of an etale sheaf. Its canonical sum comparison is invertible since inverse image is left adjoint. Compose its inverse with the sum of these sheaf isomorphisms and the homology sum comparison. This proves classical coproduct closure. Zero is inverse image of the etale zero sheaf. Good truncations have original cohomology in retained degrees and zero elsewhere, proving their classicality.

For truncGE, the sum of truncated objects has the same lower bound. Factor the sum of projections through truncGE of the sum via descTruncGE. Naturality and from_truncGE_obj_ext prove that this is inverse to sigmaComparison. For truncLE, test sigmaComparison on cohomology: in degree q ≤ n its composite with the truncation inclusion is the sum of inclusions, an isomorphism by step 1; above n source and target cohomology vanish. The cohomology criterion finishes. The two required equations with truncLEι and truncGEπ follow on coprojections from naturality.

Apply [lem-pur-exact-derived-coproducts] to comparison inverse image. Exactness and ordinary coproduct preservation come from [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. This gives preservation by its unbounded exact derived functor with the specified canonical comparison.

Regard L_s as a D+ object using the lower bound a. The derived unit is invertible by [sk-prop-sf-comparison]. Apply the bounded-below counit clause of [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence]. Its ClassicalPlus hypothesis follows from step 2 and the continuity-map criterion in [sk-thm-pe-classical-sheaves]. Define B_s by derived comparison direct image on D+. The included counit and mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompatibility give F_X(B_s) ≅ L_s. Faithful exact inverse image reflects zero homology by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], so B_s has both bounds. This constructs the origins from existing functors and counits.

Properness gives qcqs. Step 1 keeps the lower bound on the sum of origins. Apply [lem-sfb-unbounded-direct-image-bounded-below] to B_s and their sum. Define theta_s and Theta as asIso of the actual unbounded mate; their hom equations are reflexive. Define t as inverse canonical inverse-image sum comparison followed by the sum of origin isomorphisms. Its coprojection equation follows from map_ι_comp_inv_sigmaComparison and Sigma.ι_mapIso_hom.

Let d be the sum of G(i_s) inverse followed by theta_s inverse; it is the hom of a sum of isomorphisms. Test the requested composite on each coprojection. Canonical sum comparisons turn it into G(i_s) inverse, theta_s inverse, F_Y(E(iota_s)), Theta and G(t). Naturality of unboundedDirectImageComparisonMap at iota_s replaces its middle pair with theta_s followed by G(F_X(iota_s)). Cancel theta_s, use the equation for t, and cancel i_s. The result is G of the coprojection into the sum of L, the component of sigmaComparison G L. The universal property proves equality. Each factor is invertible using the etale preservation hypothesis, so sigmaComparison G L is invertible. The calculations also apply to the empty family.

Step 9: the empty family. Small cases checked: empty family, singleton, a=b, zero ring, f=id.
